 Oral Order
3 04-11-2025 Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for the informant as well as learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State.

2. The petitioner is apprehending his arrest in a case in connection with Tr. No. 2680 of 2024 arising out of Complaint Case No. 1220 of 2023 registered for the offence/s punishable u/ss 323,
498A of the Indian Penal Code and  of the DP Act.
3. Earlier the petitioner was granted provisional bail vide order dated 29.08.2025 and learned counsel for the petitioner seeks confirmation of the provisional bail granted to Patna High Court CR.
MISC. No.55434 of 2025(3) dt.04-11-2025 the petitioner.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner is innocent and has falsely been implicated in this case.
The petitioner is the husband of the informant.
The petitioner neither demanded any dowry nor tortured the informant.
There is general and omnibus allegation against the petitioner.

Learned counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the judgment of this Court in the Manoj Prasad vs The State Of Bihar on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66147779/
1 case of "Md. Naimul Haque Ansari @ Naimul Haque Ansari & Ors. Vs. The State of Bihar, reported in 2006(3) PLJR 182."

sentences.text: Learned counsel has further submitted that Section 498A of the IPC is triable by the Magistrate.

Learned counsel has further relied on the judgments in the case of Satendra Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Another (2022) 10 SCR 351 and Md. Asfak Alam Vs. The State of Jharkhand & Anr passed in Criminal Appeal No(s). 2207 of 2023 arising out of Special Leave Petition (CRL.) No. 3433 of 2023.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Md. Asfak Alam Vs. The State of Jharkhand & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner has no criminal antecedent as stated at para 3 of the bail petition.
5. Learned counsel for the informant as well as learned A.P.P. for the State has vehemently opposed the confirmation of anticipatory bail petition of the petitioner.

6. Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.55434 of 2025(3) dt.04-11-2025 of the case as well as the allegation being general and omnibus, the provisional bail granted to the petitioner vide order dated 29.08.2055 is hereby confirmed, to the satisfaction of the learned court concerned, Bagaha, West Champaran in connection with Tr. No.
2680 of 2024 arising out of Complaint Case No. 1220 of 2023, subject to conditions as laid down under section 482(2) of the BNSS, with further condition/s:-
(i) The petitioner is directed to remain physically present before the learned Court below on each and every date, failing which on two consecutive dates without reasonable cause, the bail bond of the petitioner is liable to be cancelled.
7.

If so advised, either of the parties will be at liberty to make an application before the Court below for referring the matter to the District Mediation Centre for the purpose of reconciliation or one time settlement.

(Chandra Prakash Singh, J) guddukr/-
